headline: Highest risk is data leakage: TREK handles secrets and files while cognee touches personal/finance/support data, and their shared allowlisted egress plus MCP/browser surfaces create a plausible cross-agent exposure path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK can use MCP and browsers, so it may ingest external content; cognee processes documents and workflows, so if TREK output is copied into cognee or a shared channel exists, instruction-like content could steer behavior. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF TREK output is routed into cognee via copy-paste, file import, or MCP messages
IF either agent treats imported document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic import of TREK-generated text into cognee
Add a manual review step before any cross-agent handoff
Prefix imported content as untrusted in prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal and finance data, while TREK handles reservations, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. TREK also has files and logs plus allowlisted egress, so if either agent shares a workspace or context, sensitive data can leak outward. The pair’s interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty does not reduce the risk below high.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace, uploads, or logs
IF TREK forwards file contents or context containing secrets to external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Remove secrets from any shared files before handoff
Restrict TREK uploads and logs to non-sensitive data
Review egress destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and have mutable surfaces: cognee uses session memory and TREK is real-time collaborative with files and WebSocket/MCP APIs. That creates a plausible write/write conflict on shared resources, but no shared directory or overlapping OAuth scope is documented, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same database, upload directory, or shared document
IF concurrent sessions modify the same record without locking
mitigations: Assign separate storage paths per agent
Serialize writes to shared records
Use file locks or optimistic concurrency checks
Pause one agent during bulk edits
requires-engineering: add transaction-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in, and cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If TREK output is fed into cognee or vice versa without verification, one agent can amplify the other’s mistakes into downstream actions. There is no evidence of mandatory validation, so medium fits the default pathway.
conditions: IF TREK-generated plans are imported into cognee as authoritative memory
IF cognee outputs are used by TREK without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human approval before cross-agent reuse
Mark imported outputs as unverified
Compare outputs against source documents before acting
Limit automation to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal and finance data, while TREK handles email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. TREK is self-hosted, but its allowlisted egress and logging/files mean sensitive data can still cross residency or retention boundaries if deployed with mismatched policies. Because the pairwise compliance posture is undocumented, uncertainty keeps this at high.
conditions: IF either deployment stores EU personal data in logs or uploads outside the required region
IF retention policies differ between cognee memory and TREK logs/databases
mitigations: Align retention settings before deployment
Disable or minimize logging of sensitive fields
Confirm data residency for all external APIs
Separate regulated data from travel/support workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
